name: Apcotex Industries Ltd
title: Apcotex Industries Ltd - 523694 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 EBITDA up 42% to INR 55 cr on Nitrile latex margin spike that management calls partly a March war blip; NBR at 100% utilisation, no major capacity until FY28, ADD not notified.

summary.headline: Apcotex Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 42% YoY to INR 55 crore at a 13.76% margin, with PAT up 107% to INR 35 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR 398 crore (+14% YoY) on 10% volume growth, with EBITDA margin of 13.76% and PAT margin of 8.73%. FY26 delivered record sales volumes (+14% YoY) and record exports, but revenue grew only 4% to INR 1,442 crore while EBITDA hit a record INR 177 crore. Q4 included about INR 14 crore of employee-benefit provisions, INR 4 crore turbine impairment and INR 2 crore extra depreciation, which management called largely one-off. Management said the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure created short-term margin gains in Nitrile latex and some export disruption, and it did not give quarterly guidance.

financial_highlights.value: Cash and investments ~INR 160 crore vs total debt ~INR 92 crore; net cash ~INR 70 crore

segments.name: Nitrile latex
segments.commentary: Management estimates it is 15-20% of FY26 revenue. Margins were structurally below the base business in FY26 but improved every quarter, with March 2026 described as exceptional due to competitor supply issues. Utilisation was 90-100% across plants in Q4.

segments.name: NBR (nitrile butadiene rubber)
segments.commentary: Running at 100% utilisation for several quarters and expected to stay full for about four more quarters until new capacity arrives in Q1 of the following fiscal year (FY28). The expansion will almost double NBR capacity.

segments.name: ApcoBuild
segments.commentary: Management expects double-digit growth after a manpower issue early in FY26 was corrected and the distribution channel was reviewed; the division ended the year strong.

segments.name: Synthetic latex
segments.commentary: New capacity is being built and is expected to come on stream in FY28, with some headroom in the existing plants.

segments.name: Middle East exports
segments.commentary: About 12% of total revenue, covering UAE, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey. Management says the business is good but margins have been hit by freight and raw material cost increases.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than the FY26 average, though quarter-on-quarter progression is uncertain.
FY27 volume growth expected in low double digits for the full year, against capacity that is already running near full. Revenue growth depends on raw material prices and is not guided.
Nitrile latex: no capacity addition in FY27. Debottlenecking will add a little. Major capacity lands in Q1 FY28.
A possible step-up in Nitrile latex capacity at low cost has its plan ready. Equipment lead time is 8-9 months and a decision is expected in the next 3-6 months, so any capacity would arrive in FY28.
Raw material cover is in place through end-June 2026. The company is not taking a view on crude or petrochemical prices.
Management expects a 2026 new R&D centre spend of INR 20-25 crore; there is no stated timeline for ADD relief.
capex_capacity: NBR expansion will almost double NBR capacity, with new capacity due in Q1 of FY28.
Nitrile latex: new capacity expected in FY28 (by Q1). Quarter-4 utilisation was 90-100% across plants and it is expected to stay near 100%.
Synthetic latex: new capacity being built, expected in FY28, with headroom in existing plants.
New R&D centre approved by the board, with spend of INR 20-25 crore.
Co-gen turbine at Valia impaired by about INR 4 crore; the turbine is kept as backup and may be sold. Co-gen asset useful life cut from 40 years to 15 years.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume +10% YoY and FY26 volume +14% YoY, with record exports. FY26 revenue grew only 4%, so realisations were weak in FY26.
Raw material costs rose sharply in March 2026 with the West Asia crisis; management said the blended Q4 increase tracked a roughly 70% jump in crude over a couple of months.
Customers face pushback on price increases, particularly automotive-linked customers. Management called this a big concern for the long term.
In Middle East markets, Chinese latex has started entering Turkey and Egypt for the first time. Apcotex costs there have risen against Chinese competitors.
The Finance Ministry has not notified the DGTR-recommended anti-dumping duties, which the company wanted for five years on NBR. These were not in the plan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 13-14 crore employee benefit provision and why did depreciation change?
qa_highlights.answer: Three items: a new five-year long-term incentive plan (INR 2.7 crore for the year, now expensed quarterly), pending litigation provision on external legal advice, and a gratuity policy change tied to the new wage code. Depreciation on co-gen assets was cut from 40 to 15 years because the turbine is idle, and the Valia turbine was impaired by about INR 4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 EBITDA the new base for the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance is given. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than the FY26 average at higher utilisation, but quarterly progression is uncertain given the war and raw material volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Jan and Feb were already good. March was an exceptional month because competitors could not supply reliably. Some of the gain will reverse in coming quarters, and the structural part is hard to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash position and non-recurring items?
qa_highlights.answer: At 31 March 2026, total debt was INR 92 crore and cash plus investments about INR 160 crore, so net cash was about INR 70 crore. Non-recurring items were the litigation provision, the gratuity change and the turbine impairment; the LTI is recurring and the depreciation change is mostly recurring, with INR 3-4 crore of it to recur.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material cost increase and customer resistance to price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended Q4 raw material cost rose broadly in line with crude. Customers in automotive are squeezed, and management called demand destruction a big concern. A sharp fall in prices would compress margins because the company has covered its raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nitrile latex contribution to FY26 revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue share is about 15-20%, confirmed by the CFO. No EBITDA figure was given. Nitrile latex margins were structurally below the base business in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Low double-digit volume growth for the full year if demand holds and capacity allows. Revenue growth is not guided because pricing is unknown.

risks_watch: The Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Raw material cover runs to end-June 2026, with styrene now sourced from China.
Middle East exports are about 12% of revenue. Demand is falling there and Chinese latex is entering Turkey and Egypt.
Margin gains in March-April are partly temporary, and a fall in crude could compress margins as covered inventory is consumed.
Nitrile latex remains in oversupply long term. Margin recovery to pre-COVID levels is management's expectation but has no timeline.
Working capital will absorb cash as raw material prices rise, reversing the FY26 inflow of about INR 50 crore.
Anti-dumping duty on NBR is not notified, and a decision on the Nitrile latex expansion is due in the next 3-6 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet and operations, having run plants without any shutdown during the war. Cautious and openly uncertain on quarterly margins, pricing and Middle East demand, and avoids guidance on Nitrile latex margins.
key_quotes: Fortunately, we have been able to run our plant without one, even one day of shutdown because we were able to take some bold calls in early March.
Structurally, also, there was an improvement, right? Over the course of the year, every quarter, there has been a structural improvement in margins.
So, we expect it to only improve cash generation, on an annual basis.
We are running at almost full 100% capacity utilization now for Nitrile latex.

adds.what: NBR capacity expansion, almost doubling NBR capacity
Nitrile latex low-cost capacity step-up (decision pending in next 3-6 months, not yet approved)
Nitrile latex debottlenecking (small addition in FY27)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume growth in low double digits and margins better than FY26 average, but revenue is not guided; volume is backed by NBR running at 100% and Q4 utilisation of 90-100%, with major new NBR and synthetic latex capacity only arriving in FY28 and no nitrile capacity addition in FY27 beyond debottlenecking.
